title: Samsung 57" Neo G95NC Curved QLED DUHD Gaming Monitor - $1,938 Delivered (with Trade-in Bonus & Negotiated Discount) @ Samsung
body:
Deal: Samsung 57" Neo G95NC Curved QLED DUHD Gaming Monitor - $1,938 Delivered (with Trade-in Bonus & Negotiated Discount) @ Samsung

[Saymyn4me] Feel like using this monitor is really a good exercise for the neck
[sssssam] Good choice! I ordered this monitor last week from secret sale. This is even cheaper 🥲. Can't wait to get mine.
[boozed] The monitor will replace 2 x 27" 4k screens
It's actually the same size as two 31.5" 16:9 screens
(Good first deal)
[Mad Maximus] Yeah, another goal was to not have to scale Windows at 125% for the smallest text. I figured increasing the physical size by ~15-20% would let me drop back to 100% scaling, waste less pixels, be able to read everything, cure cancer and solve all the world's problems. Or at least some of those.
[okwhy] I've got a 49" Samsung @ 5240 x 1440 / 120hz that I've been using for almost 5ish years.. … just a little tip..
DO NOT BUY THIS SOLELY FOR GAMING.
Having an ulrawide seems awesome and everything, until you realise that just because a game has ultrawide support (the game extends to the far ends of the screen) it doesn't mean it's configured for it. And the majority of games, do not support it. So unless there's a game that you really love and want to see on Ultrawide and you know without a doubt is configured for it.. give all ultrawides a serious second thought. Especially for the price.
I've found the majority of games have a HUD that are at the edges of the screen and playing at a 2k resolution, really breaks the immersion with the black bars on the side of the screen. An RTS like Supreme Commander is great but for everything else, the head turning gets so bad, you'll probably end up playing at a lower resolution.
If you're going to use it for work purposes & gaming, sure I get it but IMO, you might be better off getting two different monitors - one for work, one for gaming and, in that configuration, you'd probably end up spending less money overall.
[Mad Maximus] Spot on. I'm primarily using it for work, but will play a few games on it from a separate PC as well and I have very low expectations for the gaming side given the under-powered rig. But that's OK too, as I could experiment with the side-by-side picture as well (from two different devices).
[BennyHe2018] Using a 49inch AIWA QHD monitor from BigW with my Mac mini.
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/953300
It is good as a replcament of two 27inch monitors without bezzels in between.
I feel really wide if moving my head from left edge to right edge.
Make sure your desk is deep enough so you have enough distance from the monitor. If not, your eyes and neck will be fatigue very soon.
[MichaelAU] I had this monitor before. The monitor panel has deteriorated significantly after only 1.5 years, especially when displaying white.
[jaybo] i've got this monitor, it's fantastic
word of warning - it's a lot of pixels to drive off a single output, to get it to run at full res + refresh rate you need some really specific cables and video cards/outputs. nvidia 50-series stuff has the right outputs, i'm sure others do now but what you're after is an 80gbps displayport v2.1 cable, and to get them over 1m long is kinda rare, i ended up with this one - https://www.cablechick.com.au/cables/3m-ultimate-16k-display…
there's some modes where it'll present as 2x4k on separate inputs which might help depending on your laptop/dock as well
also if you want to mount it on an arm or something other than the stand it comes with…. good luck, there's a couple of options out there, but it's a LOT of weight to pivot on the vesa mount. (a friend of mine has his working fine on a specific mount, but the one i got basically broke straight away, despite being rated for the weight/size)
it's amazing for workflow stuff, i have powertoys set up to have 10 zones (2 rows, 5 columns) of equal squares and each zone is big enough to be useful on it's own…. hold down shift when moving windows around and it'll merge over 2 or 4 zones as required, or double-click the top of the window and it'll expand to the full height and back again if you're reading a long webpage.
gaming is… fun, but yeah way too wide, cyberpunk worked fine at full res but most games i just run in a window anyway.
[toneypaloney] note sure it atl https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/813218 (comes with a 500gb ssd as well lol) 3 yrs ago but great deal stacking none the less
[TanTheMan] I got this 3 years ago and still have it and its being used probably like 10+ hrs a day on average. For work this monitor really is excellent. I also went into it thinking it would lead to neck sprain, 3 years later its nothing of the sort. You get used to it, and WFH has never been so fun before this. At work we have 2x32 inches and I still prefer this one. Having everything on just the one screen with powertoys for window management is unreal. Tips: Get a deep desk as the legs extend out quite a bit, monitor arms were a little too expensive for me, couldn't justify the 300 to 500 on just one arm. Also do not throw the box and foam away if you have the space to keep it, we moved house and I was lucky I still had it, I would have been nervous on the move otherwise. Negatives: That plastic cover thing at the back for the ports is just the worse, so flimsy and clips snap easily. Also KVM switch was unreliable after 2 years for USB switching so got an external one for $30 and it actually works better than the inbuilt one. Mind you I have not updated the software since I received it so that may be the cause, who knows but I prefer the external one anyway.
